notes: The catalogue names the breadboard's top half rows a-e and the bottom half rows f-j. The image labels them the other way round (top half j-f, bottom half e-a). I used the catalogue banks: the image's top half is bank 't' (image row j = a, i = b, h = c, g = d, f = e). The image's bottom half is bank 'b' (image row e = f, d = g, c = h, b = i, a = j).

Column numbers and rail hole positions are estimated from pixel positions in the circuit image. Rail holes are not column-aligned, so rail indices such as tn.22, tn.28 and bp.30 are approximate. They only matter as the same rail strip.

The pushbutton straddles the centre gap in columns 4 and 6. I assumed its internally joined pairs are the two legs in the same column. Side 1 is the legs in column 4: pin 2 and the 10k pull-down to GND. Side 2 is the legs in column 6: 5V. This matches the schematic.
The Arduino GND wire goes to the second GND pin in the power header (GND.2).

Photoresistor: one leg goes to 5V (column 14) and the other to A0 (column 10), with a 10k resistor from that column to GND. The manual text says 'analog input 2', but the code, schematic and image all use A0.
The LED is on pin 9 through a 220 ohm resistor, with the LED cathode to the ground rail. The built-in LED on pin 13 (used as the calibration indicator) is on the Uno board, so it is not added.
The manual lists '2 10k resistors', but the circuit also uses the 220 ohm resistor shown in the images.
